steps.text: This Group Policy client service launch by services.exe looks benign, but I want to spot-check a few of the accessed_process sources and executed_file/loaded image entries for anything unusual.
These accesses are coming from csrss (basesrv) and psmserviceexthost, which look normal, so I'll mark this as benign.

submission.reasoning: I found no sign of malicious activity. On workstation5, services.exe (PID 716) started C:\Windows\System32\svchost.exe as SYSTEM with the command line '-k netsvcs -p -s gpsvc', which is the Group Policy Client service. The binary is Microsoft-signed metadata (company, product, original file name svchost.exe) and ran from system32. Its activity matches normal Group Policy processing: it connected to the \lsass pipe and set PolicyApplicationState\PolicyState to 0 under HKLM and under the built-in Administrator's HKU hive. I sampled 2 of the 10 processes that opened handles to it. Their call stacks run through basesrv/CSRSRV (process creation by csrss) and psmserviceexthost (the system's own service-host module), and both are expected. The other 8 handle opens, the loaded DLLs and the hash were not checked. This is a routine service start that the alert flagged as a false positive.
